title: Retire legacy feature flags & decommission deprecated API paths
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need to remove a set of long-deprecated feature flags and their associated legacy API endpoints and rollout code paths. These legacy artifacts are adding conditional complexity, preventing compiler optimizations, increasing test surface area, and contributing to subtle routing bugs under low-traffic fallback cases. This ticket covers inventory, removal plan, migrations, tests, monitoring, and post-removal cleanup in the runtime, gateway, and console layers.
acceptance_criteria: All feature flags on the deprecation list (FF_LEGACY_A, FF_LEGACY_V2, FF_KV_LEGACY) removed from runtime and gateway code paths
Deprecated endpoints /v1/legacy-rollout and /v1/flags/legacy return 410 and are removed from routing within runtime-1.20 release window
Automation scripts remove obsolete rows from feature_flags table and flag metadata in config service, with dry-run mode and rollback capability
Regression test suite updated to eliminate conditional branches for removed flags and runs green in CI across x86 and aarch64 kernels
No customer-facing incidents; monitored metrics (5xx rate, latency P95, rollout-fallback count) show no regressions for 14 days post-deployment
All related docs and SDKs updated and deprecation notes published to the API changelog
steps: Inventory: produce canonical list of flags/endpoints and owners; map to repos and deployments
Commence 'soft deprecation' by returning deprecation headers and logging calls for 7 days
Create migration scripts for config DB and feature flag store with dry-run outputs
Open PRs to remove code branches, feature checks, and legacy endpoints in runtime, gateway, and console
Run CI with expanded integration tests including smoke tests on dedicated staging cluster
Deploy to Canary, monitor metrics and tracing for anomalies for 48 hours
Progress to gradual rollout across regions with auto-rollback triggers
Post-cut: run database cleanup, garbage-collect unused configs, and remove docs/SDK stubs

2026-03-08: Gateway PR #99 implements temporary deprecation header for /v1/legacy-rollout; canary scheduled
2026-03-12: Canary started in us-west-2; slight bump in rollout-fallback-count observed and traced to stale client retries (mitigated)

decisions: Remove flags server-side only; we will not require immediate client SDK changes to avoid breaking older SDKs
Return 410 for deprecated endpoints on public API after canary validation; internal gateway will serve 404+deprecation header for 7 days first
Perform DB cleanup asynchronously post-deployment to avoid long migrations during maintenance windows
No security review required for code removal itself; migration scripts will run under standard infra change controls
review_feedback: PM review (Sofia Lin): Confirmed low customer impact and requested an announcement schedule
Design review (Ibrahim Ouedraogo): Console flag visibility removed UI should show historical entries for at least 30 days
Infra review (Rina Patel): Asked to add circuit-breaker thresholds for canary to auto rollback on 5xx spike > 0.5%
QA (Evan Chu): Requested new test harness to assert absence of legacy route handlers at process-level
notes: Edge case found: some internal metrics emit tags tied to legacy flags; added a temporary shim to translate tags during transition
We discovered a third-party library (flagger-utils v0.9) that emits old payloads; PR to upgrade and remove compatibility layer opened in infra-ops
Rollback plan: re-enable flag checks and re-route requests to legacy endpoints using traffic mirroring for up to 72 hours
Post-mortem hooks: if any region experiences >1% 5xx increases, trigger full investigation and revert within 2 hours
